rationale:
Evidence: iteration 9 (sensors moved forward to y=0.075) is the best design so far at 930.9. The oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20) finish, and the slalom finishes 20/20 with progress 0.997. Iteration 8 to 9 changed only the sensor row, from y=0.065 to y=0.075. Steering oscillation fell on all three tracks (oval 0.268 to 0.259, s-bend 0.293 to 0.270, slalom 0.357 to 0.332), and slalom line-loss events fell from 0.85 to 1.0 in the sample but the slalom now finishes every run. Forward sensing is the lever that has consistently helped (y 0.03 to 0.05 to 0.065 to 0.075). Score sensitivity is dominated by completion and progress, so the remaining gains are small: line-loss events (up to about 15 points if they go from 1 to 0), oscillation, and completion time (about 60 points at most). The main risk is going off-track, which costs 500 points per run.

Change: (1) Move the sensor row to y=0.08, the upper limit of the allowed range, continuing the trend that lowered oscillation. x positions, 12 mm footprints, linear weights, kp 3.2, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.1, ki 0, last_direction line loss, and the geometry (mass 0.4, body 0.10 x 0.12 m, wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m) are unchanged, so this isolates one variable. I did not change speed: iteration 6 showed that cutting speed slows the robot without fixing off-track exits.

Expected result: oscillation about 0.24 to 0.31 across tracks, slalom and s-bend completion at 20/20, line-loss events at or below 0.9 per run, and a score near or slightly above 931. Hypotheses: (a) more sensor lead reduces the overshoot that drives line loss on the slalom; (b) the lead may add high-frequency gain, so oscillation is the first sign if the trend reverses. Failure signs: oscillation above 0.35 on any track means kd should drop to about 0.45 next; any new off-track exit means the lead has reached its useful limit and I should revert to y=0.075. Next measurements: completion, progress and line_loss_events on all three tracks; steering_oscillation and max_error to check gain balance; completion_time on the oval for the speed margin.
